(1) Normative taxonomy committed before implementation as research/specs/remote-advanced-reconcile-v1.md (commit d9e8759): five-value sync relationship (absent/behind/aligned/remote-advanced/covered-ahead-integrity-failure) with the five remote-advanced qualifiers. (2) bead sync reconcile classifies through the shared service::reconcile::classify and merges the pointer-verified checkpoint via the existing import-only --merge machinery; the merge path is identity-complete (validation compares derived wire identities, same-UUID merges canonicalize NULL-origin rows in-transaction) so reconcile leaves one row per wire identity. (3) Every other covered>live shape fails closed: exit-5 integrity refusal naming the first failed qualifier, flush-only refuses exit 4 (remote-advanced, naming reconcile) and exit 5 (integrity failure) leaving the pointer untouched, and doctor reports remote-advanced as a distinct actionable diagnostic with the stable marker plus remedy vs an integrity failure naming the qualifier. (4) bead-rs never runs or inspects Git - no subprocess spawn anywhere in src; every conformance scenario delivers the pull as a filesystem copy (ADR-009). Evidence: 13/13 scenarios in tests/r027_remote_advanced_reconcile.rs pass on current main (re-verified this dispatch); close-out record in .marathon/progress.md dispatch-3. Known adjacent redness is inherited and assigned elsewhere: r028_fork_identity 8/13 and the fork-origin 'must start at 1' validation interaction belong to the R028 repair bead; the mutating-command sweep's manifest failures are in-flight R033.
issue.description:
Recognize checkpoint-ahead-of-live-db after a git pull as a distinct remote-advanced state and add bead sync reconcile, which merges the pointer-verified checkpoint into the live store via the existing --merge machinery. First deliverable is the normative state taxonomy: only a verified pointer whose event stream is a superset of live state qualifies; every other covered-ahead-of-live case remains a fail-closed integrity failure exactly as today.

Acceptance:
- state taxonomy specified and independently reviewable before implementation
- sync reconcile merges a verified-superset checkpoint into the live store
- all other covered>live cases still fail closed; doctor distinguishes remote-advanced from integrity failure
- bead-rs still never runs Git

Refs: plan section 12 R027; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 1.
issue.notes:
ADR-009 (2026-08-16) records that making bead-rs Git-aware — detecting unpulled
upstream changes to .beads/ before a flush — was considered and REJECTED, and
routes the underlying hazard here.

Rationale: R027 already states "bead-rs still never runs Git". Detecting the
store STATE (a verified checkpoint ahead of live) is strictly better than
detecting one transport: it is accurate regardless of how the checkpoint
arrived, and avoids importing Git's failure modes (detached heads, absent or
multiple remotes, shallow clones, worktrees, auth failures on a network probe)
into the flush path, where a false verdict from a safety check is worst.

Consequence for this bead: until R027 ships, the "pull before flush" ordering
rule remains unenforced operator discipline in Git-transported deployments, and
downstream documentation carries it as a standing rule. ADR-009 also asks that
R027's specification describe the Git-transported workflow it reconciles, so the
hazard is documented in-project rather than only downstream.
issue.title: R027: Remote-advanced checkpoint reconcile (bead sync reconcile)
